subject: alebrije
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: alebrije jaguar-eagle.
Style: Oaxacan alebrije painted wood.
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module for a fantastical alebrije creature—a jaguar-eagle hybrid in Oaxacan painted wood style, combining a jaguar body with eagle wings and head, aiming for a manageable 600-900 lines since I won't get to iterate.

I'm sketching out proportions and the skeleton structure: setting up the coordinate system, placing hip and chest joints along a spine chain, then extending a neck chain upward from the chest toward where the eagle head will attach.

I continue adding the head, jaw, and a curling tail chain off the hips, then work out leg placement—deciding whether to blend jaguar paws with eagle talons on the front legs, and settling on two-bone IK for front legs and three-bone IK for the hind legs.

Defining leg chains and foot helper...

For the hind leg I'll use a four-point chain (hip, knee, hock, foot) giving three spans, with the knee bending forward and the hock bending back to mimic a jaguar's natural joint articulation.

For wings, I'm planning a chain from a shoulder point on the back out sideways, using arm bones to build the spread rest pose typical of an eagle.

Each wing needs feathers—primaries, secondaries, and covert rows—built as flat extruded shapes oriented along fan directions from the hand and forearm, colored realistically across roughly 2.8m of total span.

Still writing feather geometry...

Working out the basis vectors for each feather so x stays perpendicular to the wing plane normal and dir, with y derived from a double cross product to keep everything orthogonal—using the identity that N×(N×dir) reduces to -dir when N is a unit vector.

Now I'm planning the wing bone hierarchy, using explicit bone names for primaries and secondaries attached to the hand and forearm joints respectively, and sketching a chain of shoulder-elbow-wrist-tip points to define the wing skeleton spans.

I'm roughing out the wing body as a tapered, fur-covered sweep, then layering covert feather rows along the arm with extruded cards, estimating roughly 27 parts per wing for primaries, secondaries, and coverts. I'm also working out the geometry for feather fan directions across a tilted wing plane, extended sideways and swept back.

Still writing fan geometry...

Adding covert feather rows and coverts placement along the wing...

To avoid z-fighting between overlapping feather layers, I'll stagger primaries, coverts, and tertials with small vertical offsets. For the head, I'm going with an eagle head—hooked beak, radiating crest, big eyes—on the jaguar body with painted spots, since that combination reads more clearly as an alebrije than a pure jaguar face.

I'm setting up the head joint at the neck, oriented forward, and using local axes (forward/up/left) to position pieces relative to it, confirming signed values are fine for left/right placement. Then I'm building the skull as a scaled sphere with face paint, and starting the hooked beak as a curved swept shape tapering to a point.

Still writing beak geometry...

For the lower beak, I'm setting up a jaw joint parented to the head, angled slightly downward and forward, with its own capsule shape bone-rigged to the jaw and a possible small red interior detail for the mouth.

For the eyes, I'm planning large round sockets on either side of the beak base using sphere geometry, then layering a flat circular disc textured with a colorful alebrije-style eye pattern — concentric pink, turquoise, and yellow rings with a black pupil, white highlight, and eyelash dots — rather than trying to wrap a texture around the whole sphere.

Still working out the decal placement...

For the decal, I'll pass the hit's point directly and set an explicit forward-facing direction rather than relying on the surface normal, since reading it from the front would look foreshortened otherwise. For the brow, I'm thinking a wedge-shaped sweep in a darker tone above the eye to give the eagle a fiercer look.

To avoid null hits from the decal lookup, I'll use the skin's nearest-surface-point method on a local coordinate instead of a raw hit test, which should reliably return a valid attachment point for placing the decal.

For the crest, I'm picturing a radiating ring of feather-blade extrusions standing up and back from the top of the head, like a vivid headdress crown.

Working out the fan geometry for nine blades spread laterally across a plane, computing direction vectors and plane normals so the crest fans forward and is visible to the viewer.

I'm also thinking of adding small rounded jaguar ears behind the eagle crest for a hybrid look, plus a feathery ruff collar around the neck base—using the same feather-blade helper arranged in a ring of about fourteen blades sweeping backward.

Working out the ring orientation for the ruff is tricky since I need each blade's broad face oriented tangent to the neck rather than radial, so I may abandon the ring helper and loop manually around the neck axis instead, computing angles directly.

Actually, cards might be the better approach here—feather SVG textures scattered as double-sided cards along the neck sweep surface, with lean, flow, and size parameters to simulate feathers lying back and down. I'll use cards for the neck ruff and body fringe while keeping extrudes for the wings, crest, and tail, with a turquoise-and-ink feather texture design.

Now I'm figuring out the body structure: sweeping along a spine chain from hips to chest using an ellipse radius function, with the path curving from the hip position up to the chest, keeping it continuous with the hip area.

For the spine chain itself, I'm deciding to use `count: 3` resampling by arc length rather than naming joints manually, so the three spine joints get auto-generated. The hips become the root spine joint at the starting point, acting as the pelvis anchor for the rest of the chain.

Now for the tail, I'm curving it upward from the hips through a series of points to create an S-shaped curl, tapering the radius from thick at the base to thin at the tip, and planning to cap it with a fan of colorful feathers like an eagle's tail.

For the alebrije-style paint, I'm layering jaguar rosettes with multiple accent hues over a countershaded orange-yellow base fading to cream on the belly. I'm also adding extra decorative touches: dotted rows along the spine, ringed stripes around the legs, and flowers somewhere on the body.

Now I'm planning out the texture library: an eye SVG, feather card variants built from a shared generator, a flower decal for the flank, a sun-rosette decal for the chest, and a swirl flourish with dots for the haunches, while skipping the Zapotec fret and flame patterns as unnecessary extras.

For the body I'm mapping out custom paints for arms, legs, beak, hooves/claws, and feathers, keeping in mind paints share a density budget but can be numerous since they don't count against texture limits. For the feet, I'm designing small toe spheres with painted ring stripes and cream claws on all four paws, giving the front feet larger, more dramatic curved talons in a bright accent color for an eagle-like look.

Now I'm working out striped leg bands using alternating colors along the sweep, essentially painting the legs like alebrije stripes by cycling through a palette based on position along the limb, while keeping the rest of the leg using the base spotted pattern.

I'll use a stripe-based paint function with vertical rings around the legs for a simple, vivid effect, then move on to chaining the sweep geometry itself—tapering radii from thick thighs down to narrower paws, possibly adding an extra sphere for the hind leg thigh bulk.

For the body, I'm defining an elliptical cross-section that varies along the spine, with the hips, mid-torso, and chest each getting slightly different width/height proportions to capture that muscular jaguar build, plus a slight downward shift for the belly line.

Now I'm working out the neck chain, extending three joints upward from the chest with a parent-child relationship, then attaching the head joint to the end of that chain with a slight forward tilt rather than a dramatic one, since eagles tend to hold their heads level. I'm thickening the neck radius toward the base to suggest a ruffed mane consistent with the alebrije style, tapering it as it approaches the head.

Checking proportions next: the neck top sits above the chest, the head center is slightly forward and up from there, and the beak extends further forward still, keeping everything ahead of the body front in a natural jaguar-head-on-bird-neck arrangement. I'm also laying out leg positions -- shoulders, hips, and feet for both front and hind legs -- making sure the hind foot placement relative to the hock looks anatomically plausible.

I'm now checking that the paw geometry sits flush with the ground, confirming claw tips and paw sphere bottoms don't dip below y=0 relative to the model's overall height, then working out how to properly reference the limb chain's tip joint for attaching the paw bone.

Still assigning joint bones...

Checking total part counts add up for feet, then shifting to wing placement -- figuring out whether the wing chain should parent off a mid-spine joint and estimating the shoulder height relative to the body top.

Working out wing joint positions so the fold creates a natural Z-shape bird wing (root near the body, elbow sweeping back, wrist forward, tip extended). I'm also eyeballing the resulting wingspan with primaries extended -- it comes out fairly large relative to a real jaguar's size, but that feels fitting for an alebrije's exaggerated, fantastical proportions.

I'm sketching the chain-building call that creates the wing joints with proper naming per side, plus side-detection logic based on x-position, then setting up the sweep that tapers the wing's radius along its length toward the tip.

Now I'm defining the extrusion for individual feathers, choosing which bone each feather layer (primaries, secondaries, tertials) attaches to based on the wing joints, then working out a closed polygon outline for a single feather shape with curved edges and a sharp tip, checking it won't self-intersect when smoothed.

For coloring feathers, I'm sketching a custom paint function that takes a position and surface coordinates to shade the feather with main color, edge color, and a tip accent, though I need to figure out how to pass each feather's length into the closure without creating excessive separate paint instances.

Instead of creating a unique paint per feather, I'm realizing I should share paints across feathers with matching colors by defining the pattern purely in terms of absolute y position rather than normalized length—dark rachis stripe near center, periodic dots, though the tip band is trickier without knowing L. I'm considering caching paints by palette index to limit the total number created.

Writing featherPaint helper...

Ette color combinations, cycling through about six palettes so consecutive feathers get distinct hues. I'm checking whether the paint selection is actually keyed on the extrusion index correctly.

I'm sketching the outline coordinates for the ruff cards and defining a vivid alebrije palette — orange, yellow, magenta, pink, teal, turquoise, indigo, green, lime, red, and cream — to pull from for feathers and body fur.

For the body paint, I'm layering countershaded spot patterns using the orange/indigo/magenta/teal mix with rosette styling against a cream base, then adding smaller pink spots for the belly and a simple back-to-belly countershade for the overall nest tone. For the head, I'm working out a stripe pattern mixing yellow with teal and magenta accents to give the face some contrasting detail.

Now I'm defining the head paint as yellow dotted spots mixed with magenta and teal for a playful alebrije-style face, and sketching out a beak gradient that sweeps from yellow-orange at the base through orange into a red tip, with a possible ink-colored ridge line near the top edge.

Still refining beak colors...

I'm also planning small dark nostril spheres at the beak base with an orange cere, then listing out decoration details like a row of back dots placed along the body's dorsal surface using a sweep-based placement helper.

For additional flank rows, I realize I need manual loops at specific clock angles instead since the along helper only works at angle zero, so I'll compute frames directly and orient the sphere sticks accordingly.

Next I'm placing flower and swirl decals on the flanks and haunches, finding nearest surface points and projecting them against a flank-facing direction so they sit over the spot paint correctly. Then I'm thinking through a chest decal placement, since the chest point might get covered by the neck geometry depending on where the neck starts.

For the collar, I'm considering a loop of beads around the neck using a surface loop anchored on a neck joint, letting the joint's own axis define the cutting plane so the loop wraps naturally around the bone rather than catching the body mesh.

To keep decorative extras from breaking the whole build if a loop throws, I'll wrap risky calls like loops and decals in a small try/catch helper, since partial loss of decoration is acceptable but a hard failure isn't.

For the hind thigh I'll apply a swirl decal directly onto the thigh part, and for ears I'm planning flattened, scaled spheres positioned at the top sides of the head with a pink inner surface to mimic jaguar ears.

I'm working through how to orient those ear spheres using direction vectors relative to the head frame rather than world axes, since I'm unsure the API supports word-based direction params — likely need to fall back to numeric local offsets instead.

Now I'm sketching out the remaining head features: eyebrow rods arcing over the eyes, feather cards scattered around the cheeks and back of the skull for a ruff effect, and starting to plan the eagle-specific details.

I'm thinking through the tail decoration next: banded stripes crossing the tail using the paint function's position along the shaft, combined with dots for texture. I'll skip whiskers and horns since they don't fit the beak/eagle design, and move on to adding fur fringe cards on the thighs and chest for the hindquarters.

Now I'm considering a feathery texture scattered across the body to give it that alebrije jaguar-feather look, maybe 36 cards filtered to the back area so they don't clash with the wings. I'm trying to work out how to generate frames along the spine for a "mane" effect, unsure whether the along function returns an array of placed frames directly or just invokes a callback, so I'm planning to manually collect frames in a loop as a fallback.

I'm tallying up the total feather count across wings, tail fan, crest, ruff, feet, body, head, and decorative elements -- roughly 220 total pieces -- and thinking through where the tail fan should anchor relative to the last tail joint. Now I'm sketching out the imports needed from the builder library, weighing whether TypeScript type strictness will actually matter at runtime and deciding to use loose typing where convenient, while also checking whether the glow kit import path is valid.

I'm deciding to add a subtle glow to the eye decals for a vivid effect, wrapping it in a try-catch since glow can throw if the material type doesn't match expectations. Writing builder imports...

Now I'm designing the eye texture as layered concentric circles in yellow, magenta, and teal with a dark pupil and white highlight, plus a ring of small dots generated by looping through angles to place them radially.

For the feather card SVG, I'm constructing a leaf-shaped outline using curved paths, adding a central rachis line and chevron-style barb strokes to mimic feather texture.

Now I'm sketching flower and swirl SVGs: eight rotated ellipse petals alternating colors around a dotted center circle, and a spiral path with decorative dots for the swirl design.

For the sun motif I'm planning a central circle with 16 alternating triangular rays plus a dotted ring, and starting to think through a stepped Greca fret stripe pattern.

Tallying textures: eye, three feather variants, flower, swirl, and sun gives seven total.

Writing blade helper function...

Fixing the orientation math so feathers actually follow the direction vector instead of the normal—projecting the normal onto the plane perpendicular to the direction first, then deriving the local axes from that.

For implementation details, I'll skip the bevel geometry to save on cost but keep a thin cap thickness, and I'll loosen the outline typing to avoid type friction. Now I'm sketching the wing-builder loop that mirrors geometry across both sides.

Writing wing chain code...

Still computing feather positions...

Placing coverts along the wing chain using the position lookup, offsetting upward with row stagger, angled back and slightly outward with shorter lengths than the tertials.

Defining a tail point curve...

Actually reconsidering: the full-length tail pushes the model too long for a jaguar proportion, so I'm shortening the curve points so the tail curls up and forward near the hips instead, with the tip fanning outward in the plane perpendicular to its final tangent direction.

For the fan itself, I'm treating it like a peacock or scorpion-style display -- blades radiate upward and outward from the tail tip in a shallow arc of angles, keeping the tip height modest (around y=1.05) so it doesn't rise above the crest height.

I'm building the tail as a smooth sweep chain parented to the hips, tapering its radius along its length while keeping its lowest point safely above the floor. For coloring, I'm setting up a repeating pattern that cycles through a few colors based on position along the tail.

Now I'm sketching out a leg builder function that takes a root, target, segment lengths, and bend directions, so I can reuse it for front and back limbs by mirroring across the sides with shoulder and foot positions computed from a side multiplier.

Checking the shoulder joint parents to the spine correctly, with the front limb bending back and paws sitting slightly forward of the shoulder. I'm defining sweep radii tapering along each limb chain, with thicker proportions for the hind thigh than the front leg.

Now I'm building paw spheres attached to each foot bone, offsetting the center slightly below and forward of the foot position so the paw sits flush with the ground while scaling it to a flattened oval shape.

Front claws should run longer for that eagle silhouette, maybe curved too. For extra raptor flavor, I'm thinking of scattering small feather cards along the front legs near the elbow using the FEATHER texture array, giving a feathered-leggings look cheaply since cards only cost one part per texture call. Now moving to the hind legs, starting with a scaled thigh sphere for the jaguar-style bulk.

Setting up the thigh sphere's bone attachment at the hip joint, deciding it should follow the leg chain's hip joint rather than the static hips bone so it moves naturally with the leg. Doing the same for the front shoulder sphere on the first chain joint. Then I'm defining the head joint as a child of the neck chain, followed by a jaw joint anchored relative to the head using local offsets for position and aim, and starting on the skull sphere geometry.

Now I'm adding facial detail: deciding between faceted low-poly shading or smooth geometry for the skull, settling on a smooth sphere. Then I'm adding a cream-colored muzzle bulb near the beak base as the cere, and starting to sweep a bezier path for the upper beak extending forward from the head.

Shaping the beak curve...

Adding nostril holes and eye sockets...

I'll just use the nearest-point method to find the closest surface point for the eyeball placement, since that's simpler and reliable. I need to check the eyeball will protrude slightly beyond the skull surface at that position given the skull's radii taper toward the front, so I'm computing the actual skull extent at that forward offset to confirm the eye pokes out correctly.

Now I'm setting up the brow as a curved sweep using three catmull points between two head-local positions, then moving on to the ears, placing a sphere for the outer ear shape with body paint colors at a position behind and above the head center.

Still tuning crest blade geometry...

Now I'm scattering neck ruff feather cards along the neck surface with distance filtering and flow direction, then planning similar surface scattering for body back feathers.

Still placing joints and bones...

Setting the radius taper for the body sweep, then building a neck chain attached to the spine's last joint with its own catmull curve and elliptical cross-section, placing the head sphere near the neck's top so the skull overlaps slightly with the neck radius.

Checking the head's tilt vector and vertical extent against where the wings sit on the back, making sure the head doesn't obstruct the wing silhouette from the front. I'm also writing a loop that scatters decorative dots along the body surface at varying angles and colors, while skipping the region where the wing roots attach so dots don't overlap them.

Working out orientation: since the body runs along +Z, clockwise rotation when looking forward actually corresponds to the -X side being "right," so I need to flip my angle convention for mirroring left/right flank placements.

I'm sketching a helper that embeds small sphere studs onto the body surface using sweep-point frames, and considering how to position flank flower decals by finding the nearest surface point to an offset target position.

Now I'm placing additional decals: a flower on the flank, a swirl pattern on the hind thigh, and a sun motif on the chest, each anchored by finding the nearest surface point and a direction vector, sized appropriately for each spot. I'm also planning flat pink paint for the paws and making sure the hind feet get proper paw treatment through the leg joint chain before figuring out the hind knee placement.

For the hind limb I'm defining the hip, knee, and foot positions with segment lengths and bend directions, checking that the total reach covers the hip-to-foot distance comfortably so the leg lands correctly even with an awkward hock bend. I'm setting the leg radii thick enough to hide any odd kinks, then moving on to write a small vector helper and a closure-based blade function that has access to the builder object, before continuing with paint assignments for each bone.

Writing feather paint function... I'm defining color palettes for different feather sets, mapping each to teal/magenta/yellow-style combinations, and noting that the outline coordinates stay positive so the paint math works cleanly on the extruded side walls. I'm also confirming the ring of feathers near the wing top sits correctly, that eye alignment uses the head's local positive-X as the model's left side, and sketching out the SVG feather card shading before settling on the signature for the cards function with its frame, texture, and options parameters like size, lean, bend, and variation.

Now I'm thinking through color tinting for the cards (likely skippable), confirming the rng helper's role for scattering effects, and deciding to add a dorsal mane and a cheek ruff of scattered cards on the skull with specific size, lean, and flow parameters while skipping a tail plume. I'm about to write the full build function, starting with the builder setup and random seed, followed by SVG texture definitions for the feathers.

Writing SVG code...

Designing flower petals and leaves...

Now I'm computing a spiral path with expanding radius for the swirl element, then layering ink and teal strokes with dots along the curve.

For the sun, I'm building 16 alternating triangular rays at varied radii with yellow/orange fills, plus a central disc, face ring, and small accent dots in magenta and teal.

Now I'm working out the limb and joint naming conventions for the creature's skeleton - hip/knee/hock/foot for hind legs, shoulder/elbow/hand for front legs, all tagged by side. I'm also planning the paw helper that grabs the last joint and point in each chain, and double-checking the API calls for cards, surface sweeps, and decals before finalizing the code.

Checking feather blade outlines, smoothing, and bevel thickness for the tail fan and beak details, then planning to write the final mirrored paw-making function and eyebrow rod sweep.

I'm double-checking the limb import signature and renaming a conflicting helper variable to avoid clashing with an existing SDK function before writing out the full answer.
